chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the devoutness (war') among the people, so he said: 'That which refrains from the prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.الْوَرَعِ: Devoutness, piety, or caution in religious matters

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of war' (devoutness) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distills the complex virtue of war' into its fundamental essence: strict avoidance of Allah's prohibitions. This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'war'' as a proactive spiritual discipline rather than mere passivity, serving as the foundational barrier against sin. It underscores that true piety is measured by one's vigilance in steering clear of the divine boundaries (hudud) established in the Sharia.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Al Minqary, from hafs Bin Giyas who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the devoutness from the people. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Those who refrain from the Prohibitions of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who has said the following: “I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) what kind of people are those who restrain from worldly matters?
The Imam said, ‘They are those who stay away from what Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has made unlawful.’”
